title: Observation and Scientific Thinking: Foundations
subject: SCIENCE

delivery.body:
## Objective
Students in Grade 7 will explain and apply observation and scientific thinking ideas using age-appropriate science tasks.

## Teacher Explanation
The teacher introduces the core concept from observation and scientific thinking using direct modeling, Liberia-relevant examples, key vocabulary, and a short understanding check before independent work.

## Worked Example
Model one complete science example connected to observation and scientific thinking, naming each step clearly and explaining why the answer is valid.

## Guided Practice
Guide learners through one shared task and one partner task that apply observation and scientific thinking with teacher prompts, correction, and quick oral checks.

## Independent Practice
Learners complete individual work that shows whether they can apply observation and scientific thinking without copying the model, then explain one answer in writing or orally.

## Assessment
Use a short exit task with two checks: one recall item and one application item aligned to the lesson objective.

## Remediation
Re-teach the main step with simpler examples, sentence frames, and one scaffolded follow-up task for learners who need more support.

## Extension
Ask confident learners to solve a slightly more complex version, justify their reasoning, or connect the idea to a real-world context.

## Guardian Support
Ask the learner to explain the main idea from today's lesson and complete one short home discussion or practice task using ordinary household materials when possible.

## Metadata
Grade 7 SCIENCE unit "Observation and Scientific Thinking" lesson "Observation and Scientific Thinking: Foundations".

labs.title: Exploring Plant Observations
labs.subject: SCIENCE

procedure.instruction: Take students outside to a designated area with various local plants. Allow them to collect different leaves.
procedure.teacherNote: Encourage students to look for a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors.

procedure.instruction: Have students use rulers to measure the length and width of each leaf and record their measurements in their notebooks.
procedure.teacherNote: Remind students to label their measurements clearly.

procedure.instruction: Ask students to draw a detailed sketch of their favorite leaf and write down at least three observations about its texture, color, and shape.
procedure.teacherNote: Encourage them to use descriptive language and be specific in their observations.

labs.safetyNotes: Ensure students are not allergic to any plants they handle and supervise them during outdoor activities.
labs.labObjective: Students will observe and document the characteristics of local plants to enhance their scientific thinking and observational skills.

observationForm.prompt: What type of leaf did you observe?
List three observations about the leaf you chose.

analysisQuestions.question: Why is it important to observe the characteristics of plants?
analysisQuestions.scoringRubric: 1 point for a relevant reason, 2 points for a detailed explanation.
analysisQuestions.expectedAnswer: Observing plants helps us understand biodiversity and the environment.

analysisQuestions.question: How did your observations change your view on the local environment?
analysisQuestions.scoringRubric: 1 point for mentioning a change, 2 points for a detailed reflection.
analysisQuestions.expectedAnswer: Students should express a new appreciation or understanding of local flora.

labs.connectionToLesson: This activity reinforces the concepts of observation and scientific thinking by allowing students to practically apply these skills in a real-world context.
